transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-10
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Meyer (Redwood SE), Dr. Lina Vargas (Kythos), Marcus Yeo (Kythos), Rashmi Nair (Kythos SRE), Evan Cho (CTO, joined 00:12)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick check — can you hear me ok?
[00:04] Dr. Lina: yes loud and clear, thanks.
[00:07] Maya: cool. today's goal is a short walkthrough of the week-over-week bench numbers we ran against your incumbent provider and then decide the scope for the 10k stress run john asked for last meeting. jonas will lead on the numbers.
[00:20] Jonas (Redwood SE): hey team. ok jumping in — i'll share my screen in a sec, but raw numbers first. we ran three primary traces: stable-cold, steady-state, and burst. p95 latency on our tuned Redwood Dedicated-ish config was ~73 ms for the 2k token avg prompt; incumbent was around 118 ms under same load patterns — caveat: their reported numbers come from their dashboard and sometimes they aggregate differently.
[00:46] Marcus (Kythos): quick q — 2k tokens avg? our production prompts average ~1.1k but have some long tails to 3k. did you re-run for the 1k set?
[00:56] Jonas: yes, we did both. 1k avg was p95 ~48 ms vs incumbent 82 ms. throughput sustained (steady-state) was roughly 420 rps on our cluster vs 280 rps on incumbent at similar cost-per-second assumptions when we normalized for GPU type.
[01:16] Rashmi (SRE): those numbers look good, but what's the batch size / kv cache settings? also what quantization did you use?
[01:23] Jonas: good question. baseline run used dynamic batching with batch target 32, max 64, and enabled prefix KV cache for session reuse (we saw ~23% token compute reduction). quant was fp16 for the baseline and we also validated int8-quant for throughput runs, with a small quality delta on a few prompts. note — int8 gave ~12% more rps but degraded some hallucination-sensitive cases.
[01:45] Dr. Lina: hmm, the incumbent claims they run aggressive 4-bit quant with negligible quality loss — is that apples-to-apples?
[01:52] Jonas: not exactly. vendor-side quant strategies differ; our kernel selection path took advantage of attention optimizations and fused kernels which tend to keep p95 low at small batch sizes. we can reproduce their 4-bit profile if you want, but we saw a couple of inference artifacts on sensitive prompts.
[02:10] Maya: to be explicit, this is about production economics for you — latency at tail for clinical prompts matters. lower p95 reduces timeout retries and improves UX for providers.
[02:20] Evan (CTO, joined): apologies for joining late — quick ask, what was the hardware for your tests?
[02:26] Jonas: we used A100p-40 config for the main runs, and we mirrored the incumbent on V100-equivalent instance for the comparison; we normalized costs by GPU hour where possible. for the dedicated slot we'll propose a c-similar instance with pinned capacity.
[02:40] Marcus: can you put the cost math in a sheet? we need line-item of batch size / quant / p95 / token-cost.
[02:46] Maya: yes, i'll attach the full CSV and a breakdown in the follow-up.
[02:50] Dr. Lina: on the KV/prefix caching — our chat flows are session-heavy, so prefix reuse could be a big win. how reproducible was that 23% reduction?
[02:58] Jonas: across our test corpus it held ~18–25% depending on cache hit rate. we instrumented traces — there's some variance when prompts change formatting (like extra system tokens).
[03:12] Rashmi: any SLOs — what p99s looked like?
[03:16] Jonas: p99s were 210–260ms for the 2k set. incumbent p99s were often 360–420ms in our sample runs. again, noisy but consistent advantage.
[03:30] Marcus: can you run a tail-latency test with a mix of synthetic spikes? that'll matter for our autoscaler.
[03:36] Jonas: yes, that's the plan for the 10k stress run — we'll include spike patterns and cold-cache runs.
[03:41] Dr. Lina: how do you handle fallback when a dedicated slot is saturated? we need graceful degradation, not hard errors.
[03:48] Maya: Redwood supports routing policies — automatic fallback to a compatible model variant or a lower-cost region, plus queueing windows; we can configure soft-degradation to serve truncated responses if you prefer.
[03:58] Evan: regarding security — we need to see KMS/HSM integration and audit logs before a proc approval.
[04:03] Maya: understood. i'll include the SOC2 + KMS integration notes and a link to our audit log docs.
[04:08] Dr. Lina: any unexpected failures in the runs?
[04:11] Jonas: couple of retries during burst runs because of a mis-configured autoscaler in our early run — patched. also one run that had higher latency because prefix cache TTL was set too low, that was fixed for the steady-state numbers.
[04:24] Marcus: can you make sure the follow-up CSV includes timestamps and run ids so we can cross-check our telemetry?
[04:29] Jonas: yes, run ids and raw traces will be included.
[04:33] Maya: ok quick demo excerpt — jonas will read two short logs then we'll circle back to next steps.
[04:40] Jonas: reading snippet 1: "run-id 20261103-a3; config batch-target 32; p95 72.9 ms; qps 421; token-rate 3.2k/s; cache-hit 46%" — snippet 2: "run-id 20261108-b2; config int8; p95 64.1 ms; qps 472; quality-delta noted on eval set prompt 17".
[05:05] Dr. Lina: prompt 17 — could you show the diff?
[05:09] Jonas: sure — short example, incumbent and int8 had slightly different punctuation causing a factual mismatch on a named-entity — low severity but flagged by our eval harness.
[05:18] Rashmi: ok that's tolerable. our bar is no more than 1.5% QA regression. did you compute pass/fail against our eval set?
[05:24] Jonas: yes — int8 failed 1.9% of cases on your eval set; fp16 was 0.6% failure.
[05:31] Dr. Lina: then int8 is risky for us at the moment. we should probably focus on fp16 plus caching and smarter batching.
[05:38] Maya: noted. for the stress run we'll keep fp16 and add a guarded int8 run flagged as dark-test only.
[05:44] Evan: procurement will need pricing per sustained RPS and per-peak slot. can you give a simple banded quote?
[05:50] Maya: yes, we'll send a banded rate card — base committed slots, burst pricing, and peak overage.
[05:55] Marcus: anything about model variants? we'd like fallback to a smaller quantized model for non-critical ops.
[06:02] Jonas: we can route by policy — dev endpoint to smaller model, prod to high-fidelity model, automatic fallback if latency breaches SLO.
[06:10] Dr. Lina: what about data residency? some PHI tests must stay in EU region.
[06:15] Maya: Redwood Private supports VPC and region pinning; we'll document region controls and audit trails.
[06:20] Marcus: good.
[06:22] Jonas: planning for the 10k stress run: we'll do 3 phases — cold start (cache miss heavy), steady-state, and burst spikes. we'll instrument token-level telemetry and push traces to a shared GCS/CSV for your team to ingest.
[06:36] Dr. Lina: can you also include latency SLO breach logs so we can calibrate autoscaler trigger points?
[06:41] Jonas: yep.
[06:43] Maya: ok moving to schedule and owners — i'll recap after jonas.
[06:47] Jonas: quick note on cost normalization — we assumed incumbent quoted list GPU hours and included network egress; if you have their invoice lines, we can normalize more precisely.
[06:58] Marcus: we'll pull last month's vendor invoice and send it.
[07:02] Evan: two quick asks before we close — 1) include a short doc on how rollback/rollouts are handled in canary, 2) confirm SLA targets for dedicated slots.
[07:12] Maya: 1) we'll share our rollout playbook; 2) SLA for dedicated will be included in the follow-up, typical is 99.9% with latency objectives baked in per-commit.
[07:22] Dr. Lina: perfect.
[07:24] Maya: recap of next steps — i'll send CSV + run metadata + SOC2/KMS/audit links; jonas will spin the dedicated slot and schedule the 10k stress run; kythos to provide incumbent configs and prompt set; follow-up meeting week of 2026-11-23.
[07:41] Marcus: sounds good. thanks.
[07:43] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[07:47] [call ends]

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-attribution and minor ASR errors (e.g., "A100p-40" recognized as "A hundred p forty" in one snippet). The team agreed to in-depth stress run and to exchange raw artifacts for cross-validation.
